title: Hierarchical rollout controls and LTS migration tooling
creator: Priya Shah
description:
Goal: deliver a reusable, auditable rollout/gating framework and an LTS channel migration tool so teams can safely upgrade model-serving runtime and control-plane versions with minimal manual coordination.

Scope: a versioned rollout DSL, preflight checks, staged cohorts, health-weighted traffic ramps, feature-flag integration, automated rollback policies plus a migration assistant to move customers between LTS/minor channels. Includes Console UX hooks for visibility, alerting thresholds, and a runbook for on-call.

Key components we will deliver: 
- Rollout DSL (text + JSON) supporting hierarchical gates (preflight -> canary cohorts -> baseline ramps -> full cutover) and explicit rollback policies.
- A migration assistant CLI and control-plane endpoint that orchestrates LTS channel moves (e.g., v1.18-LTS -> v1.20-LTS) and creates an immutable audit entry per migration.
- Metric-driven auto-rollback: configurable triggers (error_rate > 1.5x baseline OR 95p_latency > baseline + 200ms OR quality_regression on eval set > 2%) with cooldown windows and manual override.
- Health-weighted cohort assignment: cohorts sized by host health and customer SLAs rather than naïve percent-of-traffic.
- Integration with feature-flags for gradual feature exposure independent of rollout (useful for opt-in runtime features).
- Console pages: rollout timeline, cohort health heatmap, diffed metric view against baseline, and roll-forward/rollback controls.

Design decisions and trade-offs: 
- Use health-weighted cohorts to avoid overloading weaker nodes (trade-off: slightly more complexity in traffic routing).
- Keep the DSL intentionally small and composable (no Turing-complete policy language) to reduce accidental misconfiguration risk.
- Auto-rollback thresholds are conservative for first rollout wave to minimize false positives; teams can tune after first successful migrations.
- LTS migration assistant will default to staged upgrades with a 7-day observation window for critical customers, but will allow opt-out for customers on dedicated contracts.

Operational safety and metrics: 
- Baseline computed from rolling window prior to rollout start (72h preferred).
- Primary metrics: request_error_rate, p95_latency, p99_latency, median_request_time, model-quality-regression (from eval harness).
- Secondary metrics: GPU_utilization, queue_depth, KV_cache_hit_rate.
- Thresholds live in config and are recorded in the migration audit log.

Acceptance criteria: 
1) Teams can author rollout using the DSL and trigger a canary sequence via CLI or Console.
2) Auto-rollback performs as expected in synthetic failure tests (see QA plan).
3) Migration assistant can move a simulated customer from v1.18-LTS to v1.20-LTS in staging with full audit trail.
4) Console visualizations show cohort-level health and provide single-click rollback.

QA plan and testing: 
- Unit tests for DSL parser and runtime.
- Integration test suite that simulates latency spikes and error bursts across cohorts and verifies rollback triggers.
- Chaos experiment in pre-prod that kills 10% of inference hosts during a canary and validates health-weighted ramp fallback.
- Manual smoke run: 3 internal teams perform migration to the next minor version in staging and sign-off.

Runbook (high level): 
- Preflight: validate config, run dry-run (no traffic), snapshot baseline metrics.
- Start canary: route 0.5% traffic across 3 health-weighted cohorts for 20 minutes.
- Evaluate: wait 30m observation window; if metrics within thresholds, ramp to 5% for 1h, then 20% for 3h, then 50% for 4h, then full. 
- Rollback: automatic if rule matched OR manual via Console; rollback creates an automated incident with links to logs and the last good snapshot.

Open questions: 
- Do we expose DSL authoring in Console or limit edits to YAML in Git-backed stores? (short-term: YAML + CLI; long-term: Console editor with validation).
- How aggressive should default ramps be for Dedicated customers with strict SLAs? Proposed: slower ramps and owner-confirmed steps.

Next steps: 
- Deliver RFC for rollout DSL (target: 2026-03-12).
- Prototype migration assistant skeleton and CLI (target: 2026-03-22).
- Wire metrics and dashboards in Console staging (target: 2026-03-30).
